To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fermion-loop approach is gauge-invariant and that its predictions agree with those of the complex-mass scheme at LEP2 energies.

(a) in the fermionloop scheme, the gauge-invariant finite width effects of W and 2 are resummed to all orders, (b) the fermion-loop corrections to the triple gauge-boroson vertices are gauge-invariant, (c) in the fermionic one-loop self-energies, the gauge-invariance breaking terms proportional to the fermionic mass are resummed,
the fermion-loop prescription is gauge-invariant, and that the finite-width effects are very small in all LEP2 processes considered.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the gauge-invariant fermion-loop scheme for finite-width effects in et-e- annihilation.
the gauge-invariant description of finite-width effects in the processes et-e+ -> four fermions.
the gauge-invariant inclusion of finite width effects of W and/or Z bosons in tree-level processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fermion-loop approach provides an efficient and accurate description of the finite width effects in the LEP2 energy range, with an accuracy of the order of the electroweak radiative corrections.

, in the fermion loop scheme, the finite width corrections to LEP2 processes are smaller than the corresponding ones in other schemes, and that this scheme is the one which is closest to the physical situation.
all the schemes discussed here are gauge-invariant, i.e. they preserve the Ward identities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the fermion-loop prescription is a gauge-invariant scheme which allows to treat the finite width effects of the W and Z boson in a consistent way, and which is easy to implement in the LEP1 and the LEP2 processes.

the fermion-loop prescription is a simple and accurate way of treating the W/Z-boson width effects at LEP2, in the energy range where the W-boson width is small, and in the case of massive fermions in the final state.

the fermion-loop method is the only gauge-invariant scheme for the finite width effects of the W and Z boson, and it can be applied to the LEP2 processes in a simple way, and that the numerical results obtained with the fermion-loop prescription agree with those from the other gauge-invariant schemes in the energy region of the LEP2, the NLC and beyond.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fermion-loop approach is a simple and gauge-invariant way to include the finite width effects of gauge bosons in the LEP2 energy range, and beyond.
the fermion-loop prescription gives results for the LEP2 cross sections that are very similar to the ones of the other schemes.
the fermion-loop method is a simple, gauge-invariant and efficient way to treat the finite width effects in the LEP2 energy range.
